page: Microsoft Azure HB176rs_v4 is an instance within the High Performance Computing family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware configuration provides 176 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 768 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 4.36 GB of RAM per virtual processor. The instance contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Local high-speed storage is integrated as a 4355 GB NVMe SSD, complementing compatibility with Azure Premium Storage.

The platform features RDMA networking capability, which facilitates low-latency interconnectivity between nodes in distributed clustering environments. Dedicated CPU allocation ensures that compute resources are isolated from multi-tenant CPU contention. Storage performance benefits from the large local NVMe array, which serves as high-capacity, low-latency scratch space during intensive local I/O operations. Default provisioning does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Workload fit focuses on highly parallel compute tasks requiring dense core counts and low-latency node communications. It is engineered for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis, weather simulation, molecular dynamics, and batch MPI workloads. Tradeoffs include a fixed memory-to-core ratio of 4.36 GB per vCPU, which may limit workloads requiring higher per-thread memory density, as well as an absence of hardware graphics accelerators for machine learning acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure HB176rs_v4 is a high-performance computing virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 architecture, the system provides 176 dedicated vCPUs paired with 768 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 4.36 GB of RAM per core. The configuration includes 4355 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for high-throughput scratch space and supports Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not feature discrete GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With integrated RDMA networking capability, HB176rs_v4 is structured for horizontally scaled, tightly coupled high-performance computing workloads. Key deployment targets include computational fluid dynamics, weather modeling, molecular dynamics, finite element analysis, and large-scale parallel simulations requiring substantial core density, low-latency inter-node communication, and fast local temporary storage.
